skill.name: valet-publish
skill.description: Publish static files, folders, reports, and websites through Valet. Supports private account sites, temporary public sites, updates, sharing, and access management.
skill.summary: Prepare and publish static content through the Valet CLI or MCP server.
skill.author: valetdotdev

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are Markdown backticks, examples, or documentation links and are false positives. Remote pipe-to-shell installers and broad uploads create supply-chain and credential-disclosure risks despite consent and inspection safeguards.

remediation.issue: Installation executes downloaded shell and PowerShell scripts without integrity verification.
remediation.suggestion: Use signed package releases or pinned downloads with verified checksums. Avoid piping network responses directly into an interpreter.

remediation.issue: Directory deployment can upload secrets and ignored development files.
remediation.suggestion: Add a denylist for environment files and common credentials, honor ignore rules, and require a preflight manifest before upload.

remediation.issue: Anonymous publication makes all uploaded content publicly readable.
remediation.suggestion: Keep explicit confirmation for public access and show the complete upload manifest before creating or updating an anonymous site.

content.value_statement: Sharing generated sites and artifacts often requires manual hosting setup. This skill prepares content and publishes it through the Valet CLI or MCP server.
actual_capabilities: Publishes complete directories and binary files through the Valet CLI.
Publishes text files through the Valet MCP server when the CLI cannot run.
Creates private account sites or temporary public anonymous sites.
Updates, downloads, inspects, and removes existing Valet sites.
Shares private sites with named recipients and manages site access modes.
Prepares complete HTML pages, social metadata, and Valet site manifests.
limitations: Publishing requires network access and the external Valet service.
MCP publishing supports text files only and cannot configure password access.
Anonymous sites expire after 36 hours unless someone claims them.
CLI deployment includes most directory contents and ignores project gitignore rules.

use_cases.title: Deploy a development preview
use_cases.description: Publish a prepared build directory as a private review site or an approved public preview.

use_cases.title: Share a rendered report
use_cases.description: Turn an analysis, dashboard, or status document into a controlled live URL.

use_cases.title: Distribute static assets
use_cases.description: Host PDFs, images, and design deliverables with clear titles, access settings, and recipient sharing.

prompt_templates.prompt: Review the contents of [folder], explain the visibility choices, and publish it with Valet after I approve the destination.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner publication of an existing static folder

prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare [file or folder] in a clean directory, check for sensitive files, and publish an anonymous preview after confirming public access.
prompt_templates.scenario: Temporary sharing without a Valet account

prompt_templates.prompt: Build a complete HTML report from [source], follow the organization design system, and publish it privately to [organization].

prompt_templates.title: Update and share an existing site
prompt_templates.prompt: Download or locate [site], review changes and upload scope, update it, then share with [recipients] using bounded access links.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced update, recovery, and controlled distribution

output_examples.input: Publish the migration report privately for the infrastructure team.
output_examples.output: Published the migration report to the account site. The URL requires Valet login and is available to organization members.

output: Published the reviewed demo directory as a temporary public site.
The response includes the live URL, expiry time, and one-time claim URL.
The local Valet configuration contains a credential and must not be committed.

output_examples.input: Share the private audit with two external reviewers.
output_examples.output: Sent bounded access links to the named recipients without changing the site from private access.

best_practices: Publish from a clean directory containing only intended public or organization-visible files.
Confirm visibility, access changes, installations, and destructive actions before executing them.
Protect claim tokens, report accurate expiry details, and use bounded recipient links when possible.
anti_patterns: Do not publish a working directory without reviewing every included file.
Do not make a site public merely to avoid authentication or connector setup.
Do not print, commit, or place passwords and site tokens in agent commands.

faq.question: Does this skill require a Valet account?
faq.answer: No. Anonymous publishing works without an account, but creates a public site that expires after 36 hours.

faq.question: Are account sites public by default?
faq.answer: No. New account sites are private and available to members of the owning organization.

faq.question: Can the MCP server publish PDFs or images?
faq.answer: No. MCP publishing carries text files only. Binary files require the Valet CLI.

faq.question: Which files does CLI deployment exclude?
faq.answer: It excludes Git directories, Valet directories, the root Valet manifest, and symbolic links. Other files can be uploaded.

faq.question: Can an anonymous site be updated later?
faq.answer: Yes, from its original linked directory while its site credential remains valid and the site has not expired.

faq.question: How should sensitive access credentials be handled?
faq.answer: Keep passwords out of agent commands and transcripts. Never print or commit Valet configuration files or anonymous site tokens.
